title: The Girl Past the Filters
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Narumi Hakobe, a stone-faced high school loner, secretly follows Efa, an account that posts racy selfies. He discovers Efa is his popular classmate Koto Mitsuha, who photographs him in a compromising moment and uses it to make him keep her secret and help her take photos. The romantic comedy follows the push and pull between them as both face insecurities behind their public faces.
life_message: The self people show online or at school hides insecurity, and real connection comes from being seen past the filter.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Secrets and leverage, not confrontation; no honor duels.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Teens act on their own online and offline, adults absent from summaries.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Classmates and online audience matter more than family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School popularity ranks, but the pair relate as peers.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern social media culture; no tradition in view.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-image and online self-expression drive the story.

folkways.japan: Koto's polished public face versus private self echoes the Japanese distinction between tatemae (public face) and honne (true feelings).

delivery.evidence: Outer Haven review reads insecurity themes from character behavior; no reviewer calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Any message about authenticity comes through the teasing relationship rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Narumi and Koto edge toward honesty and closeness; Narumi's isolation loses. Sympathy goes to both, including Koto's coercive teasing.
